speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development with regard to the recent case of wrongfully obtained ComCare payments due to improper declaration of income and assets (a) how does the Ministry comprehensively assess an applicant's financial situation before disbursing funds; (b) whether the Ministry conducts regular follow-up checks on the financial situation of recipients applying for renewal; (c) besides self-declaration, what other verification methods are being employed; and (d) over the past five years, how many similar cases have occurred and have all erroneous disbursements been recovered.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: As such, it is important that the assistance is only given to those who qualify.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: ComCare clients are also required to update the Social Service Office (SSO) should their financial situation change while they are receiving ComCare – for example, if they receive proceeds from the sale of an asset.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In considering an applicant's savings to determine eligibility for ComCare, MSF takes into account factors, such as contingency savings for emergency expenses and household size.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: There is no hard threshold and SSOs will exercise flexibility based on each applicants' circumstances and needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: If the savings are substantial, even if it comprised donations from the public, we would expect the applicant to tap on his or her savings first.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: MSF takes a serious view on false declarations as ComCare schemes are meant to support those who are in need and have no other sources of support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Clients who hold significant savings do not meet the ComCare eligibility criteria and it would not be fair to use public funds to support those who are able to meet basic living expenses on their own.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Given the tension between ensuring accessibility and guarding against misuse of funds, could the Ministry explain how it balances the need for swift disbursement of ComCare funds, with the implementation of stringent checks to prevent wrongful claims?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And what measures are in place to ensure that legitimate applicants are not inadvertently disadvantaged by these processes.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: And on the other end, maintaining a healthy level of prudence and at the same time, accountability, because public funds are being used.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I am confident that our public officers at the SSOs do the best for each application that they receive, based on these principles.
